advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop the unused `root` parameter from `_gate_cfg` (or use it) in tests/unit/test_llm_config_gate_root.py to avoid implying it roots the config.
evidence: `return replace(LLMConfig.from_env(), llm_retry_max_attempts=1)` — `root` is never referenced in the body
advisory.finding: The `_gate_cfg(root)` test helper takes a `root` parameter it never uses — it builds the config purely from `LLMConfig.from_env()` with everything discovered, so the argument is dead.
advisory.suggested_fix: Remove the `root` parameter and update the three call sites `_gate_cfg(root)` to `_gate_cfg()`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a no-gate test where a config's explicit repo_path (e.g. REBAR_LLM_REPO_PATH) names a project distinct from the cwd, asserting the class/chain resolves from the threaded root, not ambient cwd.
evidence: Diff commit message: 'Call sites holding an LLMConfig now also thread cfg.repo_path, so a config carrying an explicit root routes consistently even with no gate active'

test_the_gate_root_does_not_override_an_explicitly_threaded_root uses `with use_code_root(str(snapshot)):` — the explicit-arg case is only asserted with a gate active (tests/unit/test_llm_config_gate_root.py:117)

test_without_a_gate_the_ambient_root_is_still_the_answer chdir's INTO the project (root == cwd), so cfg.repo_path and ambient discovery coincide — it cannot detect a threaded-root-ignored regression outside a gate (tests/unit/test_llm_config_gate_root.py:126-129)
ABSENCE: no test constructs a config with an explicit repo_path pointing to a project distinct from the cwd while no gate is active
advisory.finding: The commit claims a distinct guarantee that 'a config carrying an explicit root routes consistently even with no gate active' (cfg.repo_path threaded into resolve_model/fallback_targets_for/primary_endpoint_for), but every explicit-root test runs INSIDE use_code_root (gate active). The no-gate case — an LLMConfig whose repo_path is an explicit root (e.g. REBAR_LLM_REPO_PATH) while the process cwd resolves to a DIFFERENT project — is not exercised, so a regression that ignored the threaded root outside a gate (falling back to ambient cwd) would not be caught.
